Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Appellant :- Arvind Kumar Srivastava,Bhaju Ram Pprasad Sharma Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Ramesh Chandra Tripathi, Advocate holding brief of Sri Shrwan Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (1) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as 'SC/ST Act') has been filed against the summoning order dated 12.04.2024 passed by Special Judge, Exclusive Special Court (SC/ST) Act,
Maharajganj in Special Trial No.117 of 2020 (State Vs. Gomit and others), arising out of Complaint Case No. 212 of 2019, under Sections 417, 420, 504 IPC and Section 3(1)(s) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Kolhui, District Maharajganj.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellant pressed all the grounds whatsoever have been taken through the instant criminal appeal through which, it has been apprised that there is hardly any attraction of sections in which the appellants have been summoned and all these grounds have not been taken into consideration while passing the order dated 12.04.2024.

4. Per contra, learned AGA for the State vehemently opposed the prayer sought through the instant appeal on the ground that summoning order has been passed after considering the material available on record.

5. Be that as it may, no useful purpose will be served in keeping the matter pending by way of calling counter affidavit and rejoinder affidavit by the parties and as such, learned court concerned is hereby directed to expedite and finalize the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 212 of 2019, under Sections 417, 420, 504 IPC and Section 3(1)(s) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Kolhui, District Maharajganj, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of 12 months from the date of presentation of a certified copy of this order before him without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties but after giving full opportunity of hearing to both sides.
6. Learned counsel for appellant assures on behalf of the appellant that he will fully cooperate with the learned trial court concerned for expeditious disposal of the said case.
7. However, it is made clear that till the pendency of the above mentioned complaint case no coercive action shall be initiated against the appellant herein.
8. The instant appeal is hereby disposed of accordingly.

Order Date :- 14.8.2024 Abhishek Singh  Gomati vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111867064/
